description: Rule families group rules that express the same move in different words. A rewrite that swaps one member for another has not removed the pattern. Each family states how its members are detected (determinism is per rule), whether a sentence made only of the pattern may be deleted outright, and advisory guidance for the rewriting model and the semantic judge.

families.name: Contrast framing
families.description: A claim set against a straw alternative: "It's not X, it's Y", "X, not Y", "not just X but Y".
families.guidance: State the positive claim directly. "This isn't X. It's Y.", "Y, not X" and "Y rather than X" are the same pattern.

families.name: Negative parallelism
families.description: Denying labels nobody applied before naming the real one: "Not a trend. Not a fad. A movement."
families.guidance: Name the thing. Rewording the denials ("not a trend and not a fad") keeps the pattern.

families.name: Authority without evidence
families.description: Experts, studies or "many" invoked with no source.
families.guidance: Keep the claim at the strength the source gives it. "Experts agree" → "Experts confirm" is both the same pattern and a stronger claim.

families.name: Importance signalling
families.description: Saying something matters instead of showing why: puffery, trailing -ing significance, "proving the value of".
families.guidance: Show the fact that makes it matter. "Plays a crucial role" → "is what determines" is the same pattern and a stronger causal claim.

families.name: Fake-profound conclusions
families.description: Closing aphorisms and recaps that restate or inflate: "That makes all the difference.", "In conclusion".
families.guidance: End on the last concrete point. Do not replace a kicker with a different kicker.

families.name: Generic optimization clichés
families.description: Productivity stock phrases and corporate verbs that fit any subject.
families.guidance: Say what actually changed and for whom.

families.name: Throat-clearing
families.description: Openers and setups that delay the point.
families.guidance: Start with the point. A reworded opener ("Most people misunderstand this:") is still an opener.
